stories.headline: Women's tennis moves its finals from Riyadh to Charlotte
stories.summary: The Women's Tennis Association will move its season-ending finals to Charlotte, North Carolina, from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The arrangement runs for three years beginning in 2027, with matches at the Spectrum Center. The association is also relocating its global headquarters to Charlotte from St. Petersburg, Florida.

stories.headline: Japan counts more than 100,000 people aged 100 or older
stories.summary: Japan's health ministry has counted 107,677 people aged 100 or older. It is the first time the country has passed 100,000 since the records began in 1963. Of that number, 94,298 are women.

stories.headline: Fewer ships a day through the Panama Canal
stories.summary: The Panama Canal Authority has reduced the number of ships allowed through the canal each day from 36 to 32. Below-average rainfall and a strengthening El Niño have lowered water levels in the reservoirs that supply the waterway.

stories.headline: The largest new crater ever found is on the Moon
stories.summary: A scientist comparing before and after images of the Moon noticed something new on its eastern edge. It turned out to be the largest newly formed crater ever found in the solar system, now named McGetchin after the lunar scientist Tom McGetchin. It is 728 feet wide and 141 feet deep, and it formed between April 11 and May 22, 2024.
